newsitem.title: INDIA: India NSE not to revise daily stock limits-brokers.
newsitem.headline: India NSE not to revise daily stock limits-brokers.

text.p: India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) has decided not to revise its daily stock price limits ahead of the weekly end-account on Tuesday, brokers said on Monday.
They said the NSE had been expected to relax the daily price limit of seven percent for leading stocks after a political crisis hit Indian share prices on Monday.
Sales in most blue chips were frozen after the shares hit their seven percent limit in early trade.

"The daily price banks of five, seven and ten percent respectively, and weekly bands of 15, 20 and 25 percent will not be modified," brokers quoted the NSE as saying in a notice to its members on their trading terminals.
"Members are alerted to take this into account for all their outstanding transactions," the NSE said.
Price movement of shares at the exchange are subject to certain intra-day and weekly price limits to prevent any sharp volatility in the market, traders said.
"This (no revision of daily limits) effectively means there cannot be any sell orders executed at the NSE," a trader at a local brokerage said.
